newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end lower on weak world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end lower on weak world trend.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carats close 20 rupees lower at 4,750 rupees per 10 grammes on a subdued world trend and dull demand, dampened by higher arrivals. It opened 10 rupees lower at 4,760 rupees per 10 grammes.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) close 100 rupees lower at 55,500 ruppes per piece. It opened 200 rupees lower at 55,600 rupees.
** Silver.999 closes 50 rupees lower at 6,730 rupees per kg on higher arrivals of the metal. It opned 80 rupees down at 6,700 rupees per kg.
Standard gold 24 carats closed 20 rupees lower at 4,750 rupees per kg on poor demand and a subdued world trend. It Opened 10 rupees lower at 4,760 rupees per 10 grammes.
"A lot of people have booked gold and there have been plenty of arrivals of imported gold," said a bullion dealer.
Gold biscuits (116.50 rupees) lost 300 rupees to 55,600 rupees per piece.
"The wedding season demand is likely to peak in May. Till that time demand will be sluggish," the dealer said.
Silver .999 recovered part of its early losses to close 50 rupees lower at 6,730 rupees after opening 80 rupees down at 6,700 rupees per kg.
"There has been an increase in the purchases of gold in other centres," said a dealer.

Dealers said demand for silver from upcountry centres such as Ahmedabad in western India and the capital city of New Delhi covering the northern region, had been very good. (Conversion $1=35.76 rupees)
